standard.title: Share dance in informal settings
standard.description: share dance sequences in informal settings
standard.prior_knowledge: Students have shared arts works with audiences at Foundation. They can present a movement sequence and describe what it communicates. They are building choreography skills using dance elements (AC9ADA2C01).
standard.progression_endpoint: Students share dance sequences in informal settings.

nodes.label: Communicating ideas through movement to an audience
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can share a dance sequence to peers and/or teachers, using movement to express an idea, feeling or intention.
nodes.minimum_width: Presenting a choreographed or learned sequence to peers in an informal setting — with at least one deliberate expressive choice (e.g. stamping heavily to express strength).
nodes.typical_width: Performing and sharing dance sequences in informal class settings: presenting learned sequences, performing co-created dances, using expressive movement qualities (heavy/light, sharp/smooth) to communicate ideas; introducing the work with a brief explanation.
wider: Perform a dance co-created with a First Nations Australian person who has cultural authority — following protocols for Indigenous Cultural and Intellectual Property
Perform a dance for an audience beyond the class (another class, a school event) — adapting performance presence for a larger or different audience

response_modes.reason: Students build performance confidence through repeated opportunities to present. Multiple informal sharing experiences across the year develop presence, spatial awareness and communicative intent in performance.

success_criteria: Student presents a dance sequence to a small audience in an informal setting
Student uses at least one intentional expressive quality in their performance (visible to observer)

nodes.label: Reflecting on choreography and performance
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can reflect on their own and others' dance performances using Viewpoints questions — and use reflections to develop ideas.
nodes.minimum_width: Responding to at least one Viewpoints question about their own or a peer's performance — connecting observation to choreographic intent.
nodes.typical_width: Using Viewpoints questions to reflect on what the dance communicated ('What did this dance make you think about?', 'Did the movements remind you of anything?', 'How did you communicate your idea?'); identifying what worked and what might change; recognising and accepting constructive feedback.
wider: Compare how two different performances of the same sequence communicate the idea differently — discussing element choices that change the effect
Use reflection to set a goal for a future performance — identifying one aspect to develop
nodes.hinge_reason: Reflective capacity — connecting what was intended with what was communicated — is the bridge between performing and refining. Without this, students cannot use performance as a learning loop. This is foundational for the reflective practices required in Y3-4 and beyond.

response_modes.reason: Reflection requires a scaffold — students this age need specific, framed questions rather than open prompts ('What worked?'). Viewpoints questions provide accessible entry points. Model the thinking: 'I noticed you stamped heavily — what were you trying to show?'

success_criteria: Student can respond to a Viewpoints question about their own performance with at least one specific observation
Student can receive a piece of constructive feedback without dismissing it
